spec_match.rationale: Emits the §3 grammar exactly (quoted URL-pattern strings, response-origin token, report-to/redirects/webrtc inner-list parameters, report-only variant), enforces §4.4 attribute validity (non-empty, ≤4096, first item an inner list), and implements §4.3 satisfies with the spec's subset-by-equality semantics.

interactive.rationale: Dynamic pattern rows, option controls that re-emit live, copy buttons, a real URLPattern matcher, and a two-textarea satisfies comparator.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index card promises the syntax builder, live URLPattern matching and the satisfies comparator; all present.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers invalid patterns (spec's skip-and-continue), the empty-allowlist subtlety (parses, permits nothing, satisfies anything), the 4096 bound, token validation for report-to, and the no-URLPattern browser (matcher disabled, never simulated).

conformance.rationale: The matcher exercises the same URLPattern machinery as the suite's prerequisite assertion; emitted headers are byte-identical to what the lab's _server.ts serves.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (Playwright CDP): emitted header verified character-exact ('Connection-Allowlist: ("https://good.example" "https://*.cdn.example/assets/*" response-origin)'); validity verdict correct; real URLPattern matches ran (good.example path matched; evil.example correctly unmatched with the honest enforced-vs-baseline wording); satisfies algorithm returned PASS/PASS/PASS on the default pair; zero console errors, 0px overflow at both classes; screenshots captured.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts ca-builder-match-ran, ca-builder-satisfies-ran with component verdicts, and explicit asserts for URLPattern-absent and parse-failure branches.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; ghost buttons override both background and color; match list pairs colour with literal match/no-match text.

accessibility.rationale: Every input labelled (pattern rows get aria-labels, remove buttons name their pattern), outputs are aria-live, copy buttons report success in their own text, focus-visible outlines.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: auto-fit option grid collapses to one column at 360px; 0px horizontal overflow measured on both classes.

openQuestions.title: Align the satisfies comparator with pattern-struct equality once an implementation ships
openQuestions.detail: The comparator approximates the spec's URL-pattern-struct equality by serialized-string equality and says so on the page. When Chrome ships the enforcement (or exposes pattern canonicalisation), compare against real behaviour — e.g. whether 'https://good.example' and 'https://good.example/' compare equal as structs — and tighten the implementation if they differ.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible dynamic form rows add remove inputs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Label every control, including dynamically added ones, and keep remove actions named.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each pattern input has an aria-label and each remove button names the pattern it removes.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive form control panel layout without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use auto-fit minmax grids for option clusters so they reflow instead of overflowing.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The opts grid uses repeat(auto-fit, minmax(13rem,1fr)); flex pattern rows let inputs shrink with min-width:0.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Make policy tooling show what a rule actually matches rather than letting authors guess.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The matcher runs the browser's real URLPattern engine against author-supplied URLs and reports per-pattern compile/match results.

summary: A configuration bench for the whole grammar: build the inner list with its parameters, copy the header/attribute/opt-in syntax, test real URLs through the genuine URLPattern engine, and run the §4.3 satisfies algorithm with its deliberate no-subsumption semantics. Verified on Chromium 141 at both classes; matching is real, enforcement claims are labelled.
